title: Pluggable Audit Sink: Secure Forwarding & Customer-Managed Storage for Private Deploys
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Goal: Deliver a pluggable, secure audit-log forwarding subsystem for Private/VPC/on-prem deployments that supports customer-managed storage endpoints and keys. Motivation: regulated customers require control over where audit logs are stored (S3-compatible buckets, on-prem Kafka/syslog, Splunk HEC, GCS/Azure Blob) and must be able to use their own KMS/HSM or customer-managed keys. The subsystem must meet compliance needs (WORM where required), preserve tamper-evidence (signed envelopes, sequence numbers), operate reliably under network partitions (durable local buffering, backpressure), and integrate with RBAC v2 so only authorized admins can configure sinks. Design highlights: 1) Connector interface: pluggable binary/service connectors for S3-compatible, GCS, Azure Blob, Kafka, syslog, Splunk HEC. 2) Control plane vs data plane separation: control-plane (management APIs in console) stores sink configs; data-plane agents in private networks perform forwarding and own encryption keys. 3) Auth: support presigned S3 URLs + STS, AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault integration for envelope keys, and mTLS for direct endpoints (Kafka/syslog). 4) Customer-managed keys: allow BYOK via KMS (customer grants service principal), or accept wrapped keys (HSM key-wrap). 5) Durability: local encrypted buffer (configurable path/size) with ack/retry/backoff and circuit-breaker; option for local WORM append for compliance. 6) Integrity: envelope signing (per-sink signing key) and optional hash manifests uploaded to a verification endpoint. 7) Observability: per-sink metrics (queued bytes, retry rate, last-success), audit trail for sink config changes (ties into RBAC v2), and alerts for forwarding failures. 8) Admin UX: console flows to register endpoints, test connection, rotate keys, and view forwarding health. Trade-offs considered: - Centralized cloud-based forwarding simplifies ops but leaks metadata to control plane; therefore data-plane agent performs actual log egress in private deployments. - Synchronous delivery vs local buffering: we favor durability and availability (buffering) with backpressure policies to avoid data loss at cost of potential lag. - KMS integration complexity: supporting multiple cloud KMS vendors increases surface area; initial MVP will support AWS KMS + customer-supplied wrapped keys, with GCP/Azure added in subsequent milestones. Rollout plan: implement core connector API and S3-compatible + syslog connectors, add KMS AWS integration, run canary in staging on one customer private deployment, iterate on durability/backpressure policies, then add GCS/Azure/Kafka/Splunk connectors. Failure modes & mitigations included. Security considerations documented in design doc and requires formal Security review before release.
acceptance_criteria: Data-plane agent can be configured in a private VPC to forward JSONL audit logs to an S3-compatible endpoint and confirm delivery (HTTP 2xx ack)
Agent supports local encrypted buffering with configurable retention and resumes delivery after connectivity restoration without duplicating records beyond at-most-once semantics when enabled
Customer-managed key flow: can accept an AWS KMS key ARN and perform envelope encryption so stored objects are encrypted by customer CMK
mTLS connection support for Kafka/syslog endpoints with certificate rotation flow
RBAC v2 integration: only admins with sink.create permission can add/modify forwarding sinks; all changes appear in audit trail
Console UI / API: Test connection feature returns success/failure reasons and last 24h forwarding metrics
Automated e2e test harness that can simulate intermittent network and validate retry/backoff behavior
